about: Bindings of the laravel and symfony corpora (benchmark_php_usage_corpus, rerail/native/src/policy_dsl/scope/php/tests.rs) where Rerail's usedness and Psalm 6.19.1's unused-variable reports differ for a documented reason. Each item names a class; each class says which side is wrong (upstream-wrong: Psalm; not-comparable: the two answer different questions there) with the evidence. Runtime outputs are PHP 8.5.11; Psalm outputs are Psalm 6.19.1 at errorLevel 1 with --find-unused-variables on the snippet alone.

psalm-type-unreachable.evidence: Psalm reads no variable in code its types make unreachable, and Rerail reads no types (docs/design/rerail-languages.md, Variables: a path PHPStan proves infeasible from types is still a path). symfony's ObjectMapperTest: Psalm infers `$mapper->map(...)` returns `never` (NoValue `All possible types for this assignment were invalidated`) and reports every assertion after it UnevaluatedCode, so the assigned variable is 'unused'; the assertions run in symfony's own suite. The other direction: after `$this->markTestSkipped(...)` or `markTestIncomplete(...)` (return type never) Psalm analyses nothing, while Rerail, which does not resolve the callee's return type, reads on.

psalm-finally-after-return.evidence: A `finally` runs after a `return` in its `try` and reads what the try assigned. `function f(bool $c) { $done = false; try { if ($c) { $done = true; return; } } finally { echo $done ? 'done' : 'not'; } } f(true);` prints `done`; Psalm reports `$done = true` UnusedVariable.

psalm-catch-reads.evidence: A catch reads what its try assigned before something threw: a binding made before the throwing call (`$isTimeout = false; try { $isTimeout = $chunk->isTimeout(); ... } catch (TransportExceptionInterface) { if ($isTimeout) ... }`: isTimeout() throws the transport error the catch handles), or before a `throw` (`$submittedData = null; throw new TransformationFailedException(...)` caught by `catch (TransformationFailedException $e)` that reads `$submittedData`). `function g(callable $f) { $t = 'before'; try { $t = $f(); } catch (RuntimeException $e) { echo $t; } } g(fn () => throw new RuntimeException());` prints `before`. Rerail lets every statement of a try throw (docs/design/rerail-languages.md), so a foreach value overwritten only inside the try (`$v = $byLifetime[$lifetime][$id]`, which throws under symfony's ErrorHandler, which turns the undefined-key warning into an ErrorException) still reaches the catch's `get_debug_type($v)`.

psalm-condition-assignment.evidence: An assignment inside a condition is read where the condition's outcome leads: `function n(bool $has, callable $f) { if (!($has && $d = $f())) { echo $has && null === $d ? '~' : '[]'; } } n(true, fn () => null);` prints `~`; `while (!$s = array_shift($q)) {} echo $s;` prints the first truthy element; `$m = false; if ($on && ($m = f())) { continue; } ... if ($m)` reads the false result. Psalm narrows the condition and reports the assignment unused.

psalm-transitive.evidence: Psalm counts a read as a use only if the value it reads flows on to a use: `function f(array $in) { $opts = []; foreach ($in as $k => $v) { $opts[$k] = $v; } }` gets UnusedForeachValue for `$v` (and UnusedVariable for `$opts`), though PHP reads `$v` on every iteration. Rerail's usage is the language standard's (docs/design/rerail-languages.md, Variables: a binding is used where a read reaches it), and Psalm's chain also stops at writes it does not see as uses: through a reference (`$usageIndexReference = &$session->getUsageIndex(); ... $usageIndexReference = $usageIndexValue;` writes the session's usage index), into a property by reference (`$child->parent = &$parent;` then the collector reads `$child->parent`), into an SplObjectStorage offset (`offsetSet`), or into a variable a closure holds by reference (`$values = $claims;` read by `$runWorkers`).

psalm-isset-maybe-undefined.evidence: `isset()` reads a variable some path leaves undefined: `function f(bool $b) { if ($b) { $x = true; } var_dump(isset($x)); } f(true); f(false);` prints `bool(true)` then `bool(false)`; Psalm reports `$x = true` UnusedVariable (VariableFetchAnalyzer marks no use inside isset of a possibly undefined variable).

psalm-argument-binding.evidence: A binding made inside a call's argument or an array literal's element (`f(++$s)`, `f($i++)`, `[$tick, ++$count]`) that no later read reaches is unused like any other: `function a(): int { $a = 1; return ++$a; }` gets UnusedVariable at `++$a`, but `function b(array $l): int { $s = 0; return count(array_slice($l, ++$s)); }` gets nothing for the identical `++$s` (Psalm treats an argument as a use context, Context::insideUse). PHP reads neither new value through the variable.

psalm-missed-overwrite.evidence: Every path overwrites the binding before any read, and Psalm reports nothing: `$p = new X(); try { $p = new X(); ... } catch (...) { /* no $p */ }` (Psalm keeps a pre-try binding alive through the try, the case its own UnusedVariableTest skips as a known bug, SKIPPED-warnAboutVariableUsedInNestedTryNotUsedInOuterTry), `$a = false; do { if ($a = f()) break; } while (...); if (!$a)` (a do-while body always runs), and `$mappingException = null; do { try { ...; $mappingException = null; break; } catch (ParseException $e) { $mappingException = $e; ... } } while (...)`. The value assigned first is never read: PHP 8.5.11 `function d(callable $f) { $a = false; do { if ($a = $f()) { break; } } while (false); var_export($a); } d(fn () => 'got');` prints `'got'`.

psalm-loop-carried.evidence: A loop's next iteration reads what this one assigned: `function l(array $r, array $k): bool { $n = 0; $u = true; foreach ($r as $key) { $u = $u && $key === $k[$n++]; } return $u; }` returns true for (['a','b'], ['a','b']) and false for (['a','b'], ['a','c']), so the second iteration reads the `$n++` of the first; Psalm reports `$n++` UnusedVariable.

psalm-switch-in-branch.evidence: `function s(mixed $data, ?string $format) { if (is_int($data)) { switch ($format) { case 'U': $data = sprintf('%d', $data); break; } } var_export($data); } s(5, 'U');` prints `'5'`, the string the case assigned; Psalm reports that assignment UnusedVariable.

psalm-match-arm.evidence: A `match` arm's assignment is read after the match: symfony's `#[Autowire('@@x')]` sets `$value = substr($value, 1)` in an arm and stores `$value` in `$this->value` (`default => $value`). `function m(string $v) { match (true) { str_starts_with($v, '@@') => $v = substr($v, 1), default => null }; echo $v; } m('@@x');` prints `@x`; Psalm reports the arm's assignment UnusedVariable in Autowire's constructor.

psalm-cast-statement.evidence: A cast standing as a statement reads its operand: `(string) $s;` calls `$s->__toString()` (LazyStringTest expects its TypeError). `final class S { function __toString(): string { echo 'runs'; return ''; } } function c() { $s = new S(); (string) $s; } c();` prints `runs`; Psalm reports `$s` UnusedVariable.

psalm-silent-unread.evidence: No read of the variable reaches the binding on any path (the function holds no other occurrence that could, checked by hand at each item) and Psalm reports nothing: an unused foreach value whose loop writes the array by key (`foreach ($hosts as $i => $host) { $hosts[$i]['password'] ??= ...; }`), a closure parameter its body overwrites before reading (`function ($v, array $a, Stub $s, $isNested) { ... $a[$k] = $s = new CutStub($v); ... }`), one a closure never reads (`fn (CacheItemInterface $item) => 'computed data'`). Psalm 6.19.1 reports the same shapes on a snippet of its own (`foreach ($hosts as $i => $host) { $hosts[$i]['p'] ??= 1; }` gets UnusedForeachValue), so its silence in the corpus file comes from its analysis of the surrounding file, not from a reading of the binding.

unreachable-binding.evidence: No path reaches the binding, so no read reaches it either and Rerail claims it unused; Psalm does not analyse code it finds unreachable. `for ($a = 1; $a <= $attempts; $a++) { ...; return $result; }` (laravel's SqlServerConnection::transaction) returns or throws in every iteration, so `$a++` never runs.

psalm-zero-iteration.evidence: A loop may run zero times, leaving the value assigned before it: symfony's FormPass sets `$extendsTypes = false`, sets it true inside `foreach ($typeExtensionClass::getExtendedTypes() as ...)`, and throws `if (!$extendsTypes)` (its own test FormPassTest::testAddTaggedFormTypeExtensionWithoutExtendingAnyType, which expects that InvalidArgumentException, takes that path). `function z(iterable $t) { $e = false; foreach ($t as $x) { $e = true; } var_export($e); } z([]);` prints `false`; Psalm reports the `false` assignment UnusedVariable in FormPass.
